questions.text: Consider floorplanning. A. Macro arrangement matters. B. Routing and power space matter. C. Functional equivalence alone determines every physical coordinate. Which statements are correct?
options: A and C only
B only
A, B and C
A and B only

questions.text: Consider a standard-cell core region. A. It is a physical implementation region inside the die. B. Its usable area can be reduced by macros or blockages. C. It is simply the sum of RTL source-file sizes. Which statements are correct?
options: B and C only
A and B only
A only
A, B and C

questions.text: Consider core-to-die planning margins. A. Boundary and I/O needs can matter. B. Power structures can need space. C. Every process and design requires exactly the same margin. Which statements are correct?
options: A and B only
B only
A, B and C
A and C only

questions.text: If standard-cell area is 60,000 square micrometres and the available placement region is 100,000 square micrometres, utilization is what?
For 80,000 square micrometres of cells at a target 50% utilization in an otherwise unobstructed region, required region area is what?
options: 80,000 square micrometres
200,000 square micrometres
160,000 square micrometres
40,000 square micrometres

questions.text: Why is targeting 100% standard-cell utilization often impractical?
options: Routing, placement flexibility and other physical needs require space.
Cells do not occupy physical area.
Full utilization always guarantees minimum delay.
Every library forbids any placement above 10%.

questions.text: What is aspect ratio in a rectangular floorplan when defined as height/width?
options: The number of cells divided by die cost.
Clock period divided by input delay.
The core height divided by its width.
Total wire resistance divided by voltage.

questions.text: A rectangular core has area 40,000 square micrometres and height/width=1. What are its dimensions?
options: 400 by 400 micrometres.
20 by 20 micrometres.
200 by 200 micrometres.
100 by 400 micrometres.

questions.text: A core is 100 by 200 micrometres. What is height/width if height is 200?
Why consider macro pin locations during macro placement?
options: Pins have no relationship to connected nets.
Macro rotation never affects access.
Every macro pin is automatically shorted to every other pin.
Pin access and connectivity influence routing feasibility and delay.

questions.text: What is a placement halo around a macro commonly used for?
options: Record its source file's date.
Define an extra scan state bit.
Add a new Boolean output.
Reserve separation or keepout space for access and physical constraints.

questions.text: What is a macro channel?
options: Space between large blocks that can provide routing or other required resources.
A manufacturing wafer defect.
A Verilog always block.
A software message queue necessarily.

questions.text: Why can abutting macros without access planning be problematic?
options: Connected pins and routing resources may become inaccessible or congested.
Macro edges automatically form every required signal connection.
Physical space never affects routing.
Pin shapes are unrelated to connectivity.

questions.text: What is a placement blockage?
options: A physical region restricting placement of selected objects.
A source-code syntax error only.
A required all-zero scan pattern.
A property that proves no timing path exists.

questions.text: What is a routing blockage?
options: A guarantee that every net is already connected.
A restriction on routing resources in a specified region or layer.
A prohibition on all logic simulation.
An instruction to delete the netlist.

questions.text: What is a primary purpose of a power delivery network (PDN)?
options: Replace the signal-routing network entirely.
Define every state-transition relation.
Deliver power and ground to cells with acceptable electrical behavior.
Execute all testbench instructions.

questions.text: Why are mesh or grid PDN structures useful?
options: They remove every need for power analysis.
Multiple current paths can improve distribution robustness and lower effective delivery impedance.
They make wire resistance exactly zero.
They guarantee no routing-resource trade-off.

questions.text: What is static IR drop?
options: Voltage drop caused by current through resistive supply paths.
A mandatory clock phase difference.
The number of registers in a binary counter.
A measure of source-code indentation.

questions.text: A supply path has resistance 0.2 ohm and current 0.1 A. What is its IR drop?
options: 2 mV
200 mV
20 mV
2 V

questions.text: With a 1.0 V source and a 40 mV resistive drop, what voltage reaches the modeled load?
Which change reduces resistive drop for fixed current in a simple isolated stripe model?
options: Increase stripe cross-section or provide suitable parallel paths.
Rename the power net.
Increase resistance.
Narrow every stripe without changing anything else.

questions.text: Why can a denser PDN affect signal routing?
options: Power conductors occupy routing resources.
PDN wires exist outside all physical layers.
Signal and power networks never compete for geometric space.
Routing ignores power structures entirely.

questions.text: What is global placement primarily trying to optimize?
options: Only the chip's packaging invoice.
Only final via manufacturing.
The source-code line ending format.
A coarse cell arrangement considering objectives such as wire length, density and timing.

questions.text: Can a global-placement solution temporarily contain cell overlap?
options: Yes, legalization may be required afterward.
Overlap is a Boolean truth-table property.
Only if every cell is a macro.
No, every global method directly produces a final signoff layout.

questions.text: What is legalization?
options: Convert every design to a full-custom transistor schematic.
Generate a scan test signature.
Change the product requirements.
Remove placement overlap and meet applicable row/site and placement restrictions.

questions.text: What is detailed placement used for?
options: Write the initial C algorithm.
Replace all technology rules with random choices.
Refine legal cell locations and improve physical objectives locally.
Fabricate the silicon ingot.

questions.text: What is half-perimeter wire length (HPWL) for one net?
options: The sum of the rectangle's four sides.
The squared Euclidean distance of every pin pair.
The exact routed length in every case.
The x-span plus y-span of the pin bounding box.

questions.text: A net's pins span x=10 to 70 and y=20 to 50 micrometres. What is its HPWL?
options: 30 micrometres
90 micrometres
60 micrometres
180 micrometres

questions.text: Why is HPWL only an estimate of routed wire length?
options: It explicitly routes every wire and via.
It is computed only after detailed routing.
It includes all possible coupling capacitance exactly.
It omits actual routing topology, detours, layers and obstacles.

questions.text: What can a high cell-density hotspot cause?
options: Guaranteed elimination of timing violations.
Guaranteed lower wire length for every net.
Congestion and reduced placement/routing flexibility.
Zero need for legalization.

questions.text: What is routability-driven placement concerned with?
options: Only choosing testbench seeds.
Whether the arrangement leaves enough usable routing resources for the nets.
Only printing source code.
Only the alphabetical ordering of instances.

questions.text: What is timing-driven placement concerned with?
options: Only changing net names.
Only the total wafer count.
Improving path timing through physical arrangement and related optimization.
Only minimizing the number of PDF pages.

questions.text: Why can placing connected cells closer help a critical net?
options: It always eliminates every coupling interaction.
It may reduce wire length and parasitic delay, subject to other constraints.
It always removes cell delay.
It changes the required Boolean output automatically.

questions.text: What does scan-chain reordering commonly optimize physically?
options: The algorithm's arithmetic precision.
The number of manufacturing mask layers.
The connection order of scan cells to reduce shift-chain wiring cost.
The intended functional combinational truth table.

questions.text: Why must scan-chain reordering preserve the test flow's interpretation?
options: Scan patterns do not depend on chain ordering.
Reordering automatically removes all scan clocks.
Pattern generation and scan connections must agree on the final chain order.
Every order uses the same serialized bit positions without adjustment.

questions.text: What are spare cells placed for?
options: Replace all original functional cells immediately.
Execute user software as a CPU necessarily.
Facilitate later engineering changes without a complete new placement plan.
Guarantee zero die area.

questions.text: Why can spare-cell placement location matter?
options: A later ECO needs accessible nearby resources and routable connections.
Spare cells are not physical objects.
All future changes occur at the same coordinate.
Their connectivity is determined only by their file names.

questions.text: What is an engineering change order (ECO) in implementation?
options: A controlled modification to an existing design implementation.
A mandatory redesign of every transistor from scratch.
A new independent course assignment.
Only a manufacturing shipment label.

questions.text: What should follow an ECO affecting logic or routing?
options: Assume all old signoff evidence remains valid without review.
Recheck relevant functionality, timing and physical rules.
Ignore parasitic changes.
Delete all constraints.

questions.text: In hierarchical design, why define block interface timing budgets?
options: To make physical interconnect delay irrelevant.
To coordinate block-level closure with top-level timing requirements.
To eliminate top-level timing analysis.
To prove every block independently of all interfaces.

questions.text: Why can a block meeting its own timing budget still need top-level reanalysis?
options: A block has no interfaces after integration.
Every hierarchy boundary deletes delay.
Top-level analysis measures only source-code indentation.
Actual integration clocks, loads and interconnect may differ from assumed conditions.

questions.text: What information from LEF is directly useful for placement?
options: Cell dimensions, pin shapes and physical obstructions.
Only every software runtime result.
Only dynamic testbench output.
Only the target's sales forecast.

questions.text: What does a DEF file commonly describe in an implementation exchange flow?
options: Design-specific physical placement and routing information.
A waveform history only.
A high-level C algorithm only.
Only the unmodified process technology manual.

questions.text: Which report family helps assess aggregate timing violations in OpenROAD?
options: Reports such as report_tns and worst-slack reports.
Only a chip packaging report.
Only a histogram of source-code characters.
Only a directory listing.

questions.text: Three endpoint slacks are -0.02 ns, -0.03 ns and +0.04 ns. Summing the negative endpoints gives what TNS?
Why re-evaluate congestion after adding timing buffers?
options: Routing depends only on the initial floorplan title.
Timing repair automatically guarantees routability.
Buffers have no area or pin demand.
New cells and nets consume physical and routing resources.

questions.text: Consider placement sites and rows. A. They define alignment and legal placement structure. B. Legalization respects applicable site/row restrictions. C. Geometric overlap is acceptable at final signoff whenever logic is equivalent. Which statements are correct?
options: A only
B and C only
A, B and C
A and B only

questions.text: Consider endcap and well-tap planning. A. Physical requirements can consume space. B. Required placement can be process-dependent. C. These cells make every signal route unnecessary. Which statements are correct?
options: A, B and C
A and C only
A and B only
B only

questions.text: What can happen when a large macro is rotated?
options: Its documented Boolean functionality must always invert.
Its logical input count necessarily doubles.
Its silicon process automatically changes.
Its physical pin locations and access conditions change with the orientation.

questions.text: Which is a sound floorplan trade-off?
options: Treat power structures as having no geometric footprint.
Balance area, utilization, macro access, power delivery, timing and routability.
Minimize all whitespace regardless of process needs.
Maximize density while ignoring all routing and timing.
